evidence.excerpt: This paper investigates whether automated near-field scan data acquired at 3 mm standoff can reliably predict far-field radiated emission rankings before a product undergoes formal OATS testing. Seven commercial-grade consumer electronics boards were scanned on a 150 mm × 150 mm grid with 2 mm step resolution at frequencies from 30 MHz to 1 GHz. Far-field transformation was applied using a planar near-to-far-field algorithm. Results were compared against 3 m OATS measurements performed at an accredited external laboratory. Rank-ordering agreement between pre-compliance near-field predictions and OATS results was 85% at the frequency of maximum emission for each board. Absolute amplitude agreement was within ±4.5 dB in 74% of cases, degrading to ±9 dB at frequencies above 700 MHz where enclosure resonances are significant. The findings suggest the methodology is reliable for early design triage but not as a substitute for final certification. Practical recommendations for scan grid density and probe calibration are provided.
